body:
Esjeje1 wrote:
> 
> It's interesting that everyone agrees that fighting the Nazis was a good thing
> to do, but some think that what TK has done is a bad thing. I firmly believe
> that TK was fighting for a valid cause. But, let's leave aside the issue of
> whether violence is justified, and look at some social comparisons.
> 
> TK discussed the breakdown of the family in  paragraph 51, "The breakdown of
> traditional values to some extent implies the breakdown of the bonds that hold
> together traditional small-scale groups...a technological society HAS TO weaken
> family ties and local communities if it is to function efficiently. In modern
> society an individual's loyalty must be first to the system and only
> secondarily to a small-scale community, because if the internal loyalties of
> small-scale communities were stronger than loyalty to the system, such
> communities would pursue their own interests at the expense of the system." See
> also footnote 7, and paragraph 50 which discusses the lip service given to
> "family values".
> 
> Everyone has seen examples of this breakdown of the family.
> 
> One of the cornerstones of the Nazi regime was the Hitler youth. Its purpose
> was to indoctrinate the youth to idolize Hiltler's "values". Families whose
> children were not members were suspect. Families had to conform, with the
> result that parents who were against Hitler's ideas were unable to pass those
> values down to their children, and saw them become loyal Nazis. The family was
> broken down, even as propaganda extolled the values of the good family.
> 
> I'll be interested to see the conclusions that are drawn.
> 
> Esjeje1@aol.com
> "Whoso wants to be a man must also be a non-conformist!" - Emerson

Herbert Marcuse says something similar about "advanced industrial
society" in his book one dimensional man. In fact, if we compared tk's
manifesto to a more contemporary line of thought, It would have to be
that of the Frankfurt School, which included Marcuse,Theodor Adorno, and
Crane Brinton. Much of TK's philosophical outlook is directly related to 
their work. The catch however is that the aformentioned first worked for
the OSS{office of Strategic Services)  during world war two which may
have exonerated them from violent reprisal from those in power.
